story.title: You arrive at Si Thep Historical Park.
story.text: You arrive at a large historical park with ancient structures, walking paths, and information boards for visitors.

dialogue.speaker: Alex
dialogue.text: Wow... this place looks ancient. What kind of place is it?

choices.text: It is an ancient city site where visitors can study ruins and cultural heritage.

feedback.reaction: Alex nods in understanding 🏛️ and starts reading the information board.

choices.text: It is a newly built theme park designed only for taking funny photos.

feedback.reaction: Alex looks confused 😕 because the ruins and signs show historical importance.

choices.text: It is mainly a shopping zone where visitors can bargain for souvenirs.

feedback.reaction: Alex shakes their head 😅 because the setting is focused on heritage, not shopping.

story.title: You see a restricted-area sign.
story.text: A sign near a fragile section of the ruins says: 'No Entry'. A marked visitor path continues to the right.

scenes.question: What should Alex understand from the sign?

choices.text: Access is restricted, so visitors should stay outside and follow the marked route.

feedback.reaction: Correct! 🚫 Alex stays on the visitor path.

choices.text: Visitors may enter briefly if they do not touch anything.

feedback.reaction: Alex steps back 😬 because 'No Entry' means the area is not open to visitors.

choices.text: The sign only applies to staff, so tourists can ignore it.

feedback.reaction: Alex looks doubtful 🤔 because public signs are meant to guide visitors too.

story.title: Alex looks around for directions.
story.text: The map shows a visitor entrance, a main path, and several protected areas that should not be crossed.

dialogue.speaker: Alex
dialogue.text: Where is the proper entrance? I do not want to walk into the wrong area.

choices.text: Follow the marked path to the visitor entrance; I can point it out on the map.

feedback.reaction: Alex walks toward the entrance 🚶 and avoids the protected area.

choices.text: The entrance is anywhere that has no guard standing nearby.

feedback.reaction: Alex looks uncertain 😵 because the absence of a guard does not mean access is allowed.

choices.text: Take a shortcut through the ruins because it will save time.

feedback.reaction: Alex steps back 😬 because shortcuts could damage fragile areas.

story.title: You see an information board.
story.text: The board reads: 'Ancient City of Si Thep'. Alex asks what the word 'ancient' suggests in this context.

scenes.question: In this context, what does 'ancient' mean?

choices.text: It refers to a settlement from the distant past, not a modern town.

feedback.reaction: Correct! 🏛️ Alex understands that the word describes how old the site is.

choices.text: It means the city was newly built to look old.

feedback.reaction: Alex shakes their head 😅 because 'ancient' does not mean newly built.

choices.text: It describes a place that is noisy and crowded.

feedback.reaction: Alex frowns 🤔 because the word describes age, not sound or crowd size.

story.title: Alex reflects on the visit.
story.text: After reading several signs and walking along the marked path, Alex realizes the park is both beautiful and historically important.

dialogue.speaker: Alex
dialogue.text: This place is very interesting. I can imagine how old it must be.

choices.text: Yes, the ruins and information boards help visitors imagine life here long ago.

feedback.reaction: Alex smiles 😊 and continues reading carefully.

choices.text: Yes, and old places do not need careful protection anymore.

feedback.reaction: Alex looks concerned 😕 because old sites often need extra protection.

choices.text: No, reading signs is unnecessary when a place looks old.

feedback.reaction: Alex disagrees 😅 because signs help visitors understand the site.
